generated.article_markdown:
## What it is

OpenLogi is a native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust and built on GPUI. It gives you full control over Logitech mice, keyboards, and webcams over HID++ and UVC protocols without requiring an account or telemetry.

## Why it matters

Proprietary device configuration suites are typically heavy resource hogs that demand cloud accounts and telemetry access. Linux users are frequently left out entirely. OpenLogi solves this by providing a lightweight, transparent tool that stores all configuration inside a simple plain-text TOML file.

## Key features

- Configure DPI presets, report rates, and SmartShift wheel behavior without an active internet connection.
- Define per-application profiles that automatically switch based on the currently focused app.
- Assign actions rings, separate tap and hold bindings, or multi-step macros to mouse buttons.
- Control Litra lighting power, brightness, and color temperature directly from your desktop.
- Manage UVC webcam settings and live previews with automatic release of the hardware stream.

## Quick start

To install OpenLogi from source using Cargo, run:

```bash
cargo install openlogi
```

## Who should try it

This tool is ideal for developers, Linux desktop users, and privacy-conscious power users who rely on Logitech hardware and want to ditch bloated companion software.

## Verdict

An essential utility for anyone tired of proprietary mouse software, provided you are comfortable with software still under active development.

generated.article_markdown:
## What it is

Graphify is a developer tool that converts codebases, documentation, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph. Designed as a skill for assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI, it uses local tree-sitter AST parsing to map code deterministically without sending your source files to an external LLM.

## Why it matters

Navigating large codebases typically involves grepping through files or dumping massive chunks of code into an AI context window. Graphify introduces a structured alternative, letting you query code relationships, trace paths between components, and inspect system architecture locally.

## Key features

- Parse ~40 languages locally into tree-sitter AST nodes without sending code to an LLM.
- Query the generated graph using path tracing, node explanations, and natural language.
- Identify heavily connected god nodes and subsystem communities using Leiden clustering.
- Link rationale comments, architectural decision records, PDFs, and media into the graph.
- Inspect confidence tags on every edge to distinguish explicit extractions from inferences.

## Quick start

To install the CLI and register the assistant skill, run the following command:

```bash
uv tool install graphifyy
```

## Who should try it

This tool is built for software engineers working with large monorepos, unfamiliar legacy codebases, or complex microservice architectures who want more precise context for their AI coding assistants.

## Verdict

Graphify offers a practical, local-first approach to code navigation that bypasses heavy vector databases. While media and document semantic passes require configured API keys, the core AST parsing provides immediate value for local development.

Obscura is a headless browser engine implemented in Rust, designed specifically for web scraping pipelines and AI agent automation. Rather than launching a full instance of Chromium, Obscura executes JavaScript via an embedded V8 engine and supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol. This architecture allows it to serve as a drop-in replacement for existing automation frameworks while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint.

## Why it matters

Standard headless browsers require substantial system memory and considerable startup time, which creates bottlenecks when scaling web scraping operations or running concurrent AI agents. By eliminating external browser dependencies and optimizing core execution routines, Obscura provides an efficient alternative for environments where resource utilization directly impacts operational costs.

## Key features

- Execute JavaScript using an embedded V8 engine
- Communicate via the Chrome DevTools Protocol
- Capture screenshots and export PDF documents natively
- Integrate directly with existing Puppeteer and Playwright scripts
- Run inside a minimal distroless Docker container

## Quick start

To fetch a page and evaluate an expression using a downloaded binary, run:

```bash
./obscura fetch https://example.com --eval "document.title"
```

## Who should try it

Developers and engineers managing large-scale web scrapers, automated testing suites, or AI agents that interact with modern web applications will find Obscura's low memory profile and fast startup times valuable.

## Verdict

Obscura delivers a practical, low-overhead browser engine for developers looking to bypass the performance constraints of traditional headless Chrome deployments.

## What it is

Horizon is an independent, clean-room reimplementation of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 written completely in Rust. Rather than wrapping or modifying the existing game jar, it builds a high-performance native engine from the ground up that reads vanilla assets, processes existing save files, and runs standard game rules. It relies on rigorous differential testing harnesses to verify that its internal mechanics match vanilla behavior down to the smallest detail.

## Why it matters

Traditional Minecraft relies heavily on the Java Virtual Machine, introducing well-known performance ceilings, garbage collection pauses, and heavy memory overhead. By shifting the entire game loop into Rust, Horizon unlocks direct hardware utilization, smoother frame pacing, and a drastically smaller resource footprint. Furthermore, it treats programmability as a first-class citizen, offering built-in interfaces for automation.

## Key features

- Native execution of vanilla world generation, mobs, villagers, redstone circuits, and player commands.
- Built-in agent control via `horizon-ctl` and MCP support for programmatic interactions.
- Support for distant terrain rendering up to 1024 chunks alongside modern graphics presets.
- Standalone server deployment capability that requires no underlying Java installation.

## Quick start

To build and run the client from source after preparing your assets, use:

```sh
cargo run --release -p horizon-client
```

## Who should try it

This project fits systems programmers, Rust enthusiasts, and developers building AI agents who want a deeply inspectable, high-performance game environment. Casual survival players should check the open parity gaps before migrating primary worlds.

## Verdict

Horizon is an astonishing technical achievement that proves complex Java software can be cleanly ported to systems languages. While it continues to close remaining parity gaps, its native speed and agent control features make it uniquely powerful.

`ip-as-logo` is a compact Agent Skill for generating extremely simple, cute, company-ready IP mascots. It prioritizes lovable character appeal, bold rounded silhouettes, strict complexity limits, a dominant lower-left composition, and a solid named background color.

- One dominant silhouette built from roughly 4–7 large basic shapes
- Three semantic colors by default: two IP base colors plus one background color

queue.name: totk-pc-recomp
queue.readme_excerpt:
# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native x86-64 application for Windows and Linux ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.1.0, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows and Linux; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.1.0, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3; 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 saves carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- HDR10 output with peak, game and HUD brightness settings
- 16:10 (Steam Deck, handhelds), 21:9 and 32:9
